clips.start_words: I was just in Beverly Hills
clips.send: A friend chasing status symbols sends this in awe - some people really do have money to burn.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says he was in Beverly Hills watching Rolls-Royce after Rolls-Royce, Ferraris, Lamborghinis and Bentleys pull up - people in Rolex watches ordering $500 bottles of champagne like it was water.

At the bar, a guy ordered a double of $750-an-ounce scotch without blinking. Kevin asked him straight: is it even worth it? The guy's answer: no, but I've got money to burn.

Kevin says that's where the old phrase comes from - in the cigar lounges, some rich guys would actually light their cigar with a burning $100 bill, just because they could.

clips.start_words: I remember the very first event
clips.send: Someone always 'too busy' or 'too broke' for the thing that could change everything sends this in shame at their own excuse.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau says the first seminar he ever went to was taught by a guy from Boston who'd never left the state - until he flew to Los Angeles to teach how he made millions.

The ticket was $2,000, worth 20 to 30 thousand today. Kevin's first reaction: too far, too expensive, not going.

Then the man on stage said the line that changed his mind: you see the price, and the value is nothing to you. Kevin went. In the room, the rule was simple - if you didn't make a million last year, sit down and shut up. Kevin took notes, applied what he heard, and made millions too.
